o: The caval opening is at T10

The caval opening is at T8, in the central tendon.
The oesophageal opening is at T10, the aortic at T12.
The oesophageal opening transmits the phrenic nerves

It transmits the vagal trunks and oesophageal branches of the left gastric vessels.
The phrenic nerves do not pass through it.
The aortic opening lies in the central tendon

The aortic opening lies behind the median arcuate ligament at T12.
It is outside the muscle, so breathing does not squeeze the aorta.
The caval opening transmits the right phrenic nerve

Branches of the right phrenic pass through the caval opening with the IVC.
The left phrenic pierces the muscle on its own.
Begins at the cisterna chyli

It starts at the cisterna chyli near L1/L2.
It drains everything below the diaphragm.
Enters the thorax through the oesophageal opening

It enters through the aortic opening, with the aorta and azygos vein.
It lies between them.
Ends at the right venous angle

It ends at the left venous angle (left subclavian and internal jugular).
The right lymphatic duct drains the right side of head, neck, chest and arm.
Crosses behind the left internal jugular vein at T4

It arches behind the carotid sheath at C7 to reach the left internal jugular.
It crosses from right to left at T5. (Last's p. 438)
Drains into the left brachiocephalic vein

It drains into the superior vena cava.
The left superior intercostal vein drains into the left brachiocephalic.
Arches over the root of the right lung

It arches forward over the right lung root at T4.
It then joins the SVC.
Receives the left superior intercostal vein

The left superior intercostal drains into the left brachiocephalic vein.
The azygos receives the right superior intercostal vein.
Enters the thorax through the aortic opening

It usually enters through the aortic opening, on the right of the thoracic duct.
It may pierce the right crus instead.
T1 gives a large branch to the brachial plexus

Most of T1 joins the brachial plexus.
Its intercostal branch is small.
The lower intercostal nerves supply the anterior abdominal wall

T7–T11 continue into the abdominal wall.
So chest disease can mimic abdominal pain.
Each nerve lies lowest in the neurovascular bundle

From above down: vein, artery, nerve.
So needles go just above a rib.
They run between the internal and innermost intercostal muscles

The neurovascular plane is between internal and innermost intercostals.
This matches the plane in the abdominal wall.
Has a left recurrent laryngeal branch hooking round the subclavian artery

The left recurrent hooks round the arch of the aorta, behind the ligamentum arteriosum.
The right hooks round the subclavian.
Passes in front of the lung roots

The vagi pass behind the lung roots.
The phrenic nerves pass in front.
Forms the anterior vagal trunk from the right vagus

The right vagus mainly forms the posterior trunk, the left the anterior.
This follows the rotation of the stomach.
On the left, crosses the arch of the aorta

The left vagus crosses the left side of the aortic arch.
It lies behind the left phrenic nerve here.
Comes from C3, C4 and C5

Mainly C4.
So high cord lesions can paralyse the diaphragm.
Passes behind the lung root

It passes in front of the lung root.
The vagus passes behind.
On the left, passes through the caval opening

The left phrenic pierces the muscle of the left dome on its own.
Branches of the right phrenic pass through the caval opening.
Supplies the intercostal muscles

It is the only motor nerve to the diaphragm.
The intercostal muscles are supplied by intercostal nerves.

questions.s: At the level of the sternal angle:
o: The plane passes above the arch of the aorta

The arch begins and ends at this plane and lies wholly above it, in the superior mediastinum.
So the plane runs below the arch, not above it.
The trachea bifurcates

The bifurcation is at about T4/5 in the cadaver.
It moves lower in deep inspiration.
The plane passes through T7

The plane passes through the T4/5 disc.
It divides superior from inferior mediastinum.
The second costal cartilage joins the sternum

The second costal cartilage is the landmark for counting ribs.
Count down from it.
The parietal pleura is supplied by the vagus

Costal pleura is supplied by intercostal nerves; mediastinal and central diaphragmatic pleura by the phrenic.
That is why pleurisy can cause shoulder-tip pain.
The visceral pleura is sensitive to pain

Visceral pleura has only autonomic supply and is insensitive to pain.
Pain means the parietal pleura is involved.
The lung extends lower than the pleura

The pleura reaches about two ribs below the lung in quiet breathing.
This is the costodiaphragmatic recess.
The suprapleural membrane is attached to the transverse process of C7

It covers the cervical pleura from the C7 transverse process to the inner first rib.
It protects the pleura at the root of the neck.
